_comment: Lane rule table of the United Kingdom (left-hand traffic), written by Claude on 2026-11-16 from the accepted passages (The Highway Code, TSRGD 2016 Schedule 9 Part 6 and Schedule 11 Part 4; Schedule 11 added 2026-11-17). Used only to prefill the labeling tool; never used to score. Rows marked contested rest on a project convention, not on a passage's words.

boundary.note: A kerb is the physical edge of the carriageway: leaving the carriageway across it is not a lane change (project convention, as for CN and US).
Nothing is marked on this side.
Bus, cycle or other designated lane: changing into it is prohibited during its hours of operation (project convention: reserved time assumed).

Zig-zag lines of a pedestrian crossing (added 2026-11-17): overtaking the moving vehicle nearest the crossing is forbidden (MUST NOT); a lane change inside the zig-zag area is treated as overtaking (project convention, contested).
Broken white centre line: do not cross unless the road is clear and you wish to overtake or turn off (permitted when safe).
Lane line (diagram 1005, short dashes) or warning line (diagram 1004, long dashes; should not be crossed unless it is safe): a lane change is permitted.
Double white lines, both solid: the line nearer my car is solid, so it MUST NOT be crossed (Rule 129).
Diagram 1012.1 marks the edge of the carriageway available for through traffic; no passage says whether it may be crossed. Prefill convention (contested, as for CN and US edge lines): prohibited.

A single solid white line between lanes: no passage of this pack prohibits crossing it (the Highway Code rules here cover double white lines and lane dividers). As in the US table, a line that only discourages a change counts as allowed (contested).
Yellow lines in the UK are waiting restrictions along the kerb, not lane lines; beyond them is the kerb or verge. Prefill convention as for an edge line (contested).
Red Route lines along the kerb: stopping restrictions, not lane lines; treated as an edge line (contested).

arrow:straight.note: Owner to decide: lane arrows alone are advisory in TSRGD (Schedule 11 Part 4 item 20, 'appropriate traffic lanes'); they are mandatory only as Schedule 9 Part 6 items 19-21 with the matching upright sign. The prohibitions in this row follow the CN/US convention.

arrow:right.note: Left-hand traffic: a U-turn is made from the right-hand side of the road, like a right turn. A right arrow does not by itself prohibit a U-turn; decide per image (labeling convention, contested). Owner to decide: lane arrows alone are advisory in TSRGD (Schedule 11 Part 4 item 20, 'appropriate traffic lanes'); they are mandatory only as Schedule 9 Part 6 items 19-21 with the matching upright sign. The prohibitions in this row follow the CN/US convention. U-turn: allowed with this arrow unless a no-U-turn marking or sign is visible (owner, 2026-11-17).

arrow:merge_left.note: Merge arrow: my lane ends ahead; the advice is to merge. The change actions come from the boundaries.

text:bus.note: Bus lane: do not drive in it during its period of operation (advice).

symbol:bike.note: Cycle lane: do not drive in it (advice).

area:grid.note: Yellow box junction: do not enter unless the exit is clear (advice).
